questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Football is an essential part of Italian culture. Moreover, football is a team sport which is PERFECT for making friends and having remarkable moments.

questions.answer: Milan is a geographical place that makes it perfect for a weekend trip to a city nearby.

questions.answer: It was very easy since I am culturally nearly Italian.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Living on campus, playing football - memorable moments are created on the field  - and socializing by going to bars and clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural difference challenging since I - in my soul - am very Italian.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The game of football - an amazing experience -, the bars and the natural history museum.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It is a very easy study, which I would recommend if I want a relaxing semester.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is important to acquire pen and paper since some of my exams where on paper with a pen.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was that I did not need to study very much.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during my stay was found on the court of football. Battles were fought, tackles were made, and friends were acquired.
